Header:
Date: 2026-06-14
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Ava (CTO), Liam (Eng Manager), Sofia (Data Ops), Nate (SRE), Jules (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): quick alignment on onboarding steps; security artifacts to be shared; perf benchmark next week.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I know Jules and Ava scheduled this as an immersion and ops sync for the Deepwater pilot. We'll do a quick intro then dive into network and performance.
00:18 Ava: Hi, thanks Maya. Quick context — we're running a customer support augmentation pipeline, low latency at peak, lots of short prompts with some longer context windows. Data residency and encryption is critical for us.
00:34 Jonas: got it. quick clarifying q — when you say low latency at peak, are we talking 95th p99-ish SLAs, and what's your token mix?
00:45 Liam: mostly short, like 40–120 tokens per request, but we have a 10% long tail with 700–1,000 tokens for thread summarization.
00:56 Jonas: alright that helps. For the pilot we typically recommend a dedicated pool if you need consistent p95 latency under heavy traffic, otherwise hosted with routing and prefix caching is cheaper.
01:12 Nate: quick interruption — security lane first: we need to know how keys are handled. Do you support customer-managed KMS, HSM, and do you provide audit logs per token request?
01:26 Maya: yes, good Q. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS and HSM; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and audit logs. we'll share the SOC2 artefact and example audit log output.
01:40 Ava: when you say audit logs do you log prompt text? that's a red flag for compliance.
01:48 Jonas: we can mask or redact at ingestion and we have tokenized hashes in logs instead of raw prompts if you need that. there is a config for no-persist mode for sensitive streams.
02:03 Sofia: perfect — we'll need that no-persist toggle and an approach to redact PII at the edge. also need the retention window options.
02:15 Maya: we'll include retention defaults and how to configure them in the runbook.
02:21 Jules: timeline — we want a pilot in staging by end of June, production by mid-July if things look good.
02:30 Ravi: note that in some customers we do a 2-week staging benchmark, then a canary rollout. we can accelerate if the perf tests pass.
02:40 Jonas: on perf: a couple of gotchas — batching helps throughput, but increases latency for single requests. we should pick a SLA that fits your UX; e.g., 200–300ms extra for aggressive batching.
02:55 Liam: so hybrid—dedicated pool for peak routes, hosted for less critical background jobs?
03:01 Jonas: exactly. smart routing by route key — real-time lookups use dedicated, async jobs hit hosted. we can demo routing config in console.
03:14 Ava: network — can you do VPC peering or do we need a private link? what's the recommended secure path from our on-prem to your runtime?
03:24 Maya: options: VPC peering in the region, or customer VPN into a dedicated VPC, or for strict air-gapped we have Private (on-prem) package. for most enterprise customers, a VPN or PrivateLink equivalent is what we set up.
03:38 Nate: firewall rules — what's the egress range we should allow?
03:44 Jonas: we'll provide a minimal set of IP ranges and FQDNs; we'll also include an example Security Group and Terraform snippet in the runbook.
03:55 Nate: great, that Terraform snippet will save time.
04:01 Maya: ok I'm noting action items — we'll produce docs and runbook, and Jonas will lead the perf run coordination.
04:07 Ava: curious about cost model — if we go dedicated for some routes, what's the commit look like?
04:14 Maya: dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commit; we can model a mixed plan that hedges peak traffic with limited burst. i'll include a sample cost calc in the materials.
04:24 Liam: any latency tradeoffs from quantization? we plan to use a 8-bit quantized model for cost reasons.
04:31 Jonas: quantization helps memory and cost, typically minimal latency change, but bigger models might need a different kernel path. we'll recommend quant levels per route in the optimize suggestions.
04:45 Sofia: for our data pipeline we need embeddings for retrieval — how are embeddings charged and can that be batched?
04:52 Maya: embeddings are billed per unit as usual, and yes you can batch them—our SDK supports chunked embedding calls and automatic retry.
05:03 Jules: regarding stakeholders — I'll be the PM, Nate and Liam are the tech leads, Ava is approver. who from Redwood is our ongoing contact?
05:12 Ravi: i'll be your CSM for the pilot, Maya will own the commercial side, Jonas will be technical lead for the run.
05:20 Ava: good. can you share a sample runbook and a staging checklist in the next few days?
05:26 Maya: yes, by Thursday 6/18. we'll also include the SOC2/ISO summary and example logs.
05:33 Nate: slightly concerned about token-level logging — please show us an example that demonstrates redaction in practice.
05:40 Jonas: we can run a short demo showing logs with the redact config; caveat: the demo will show synthetic data to avoid leaking real prompts.
05:50 Sofia: on the sample prompt set — we will share a set of 200 typical prompts and mark high-risk ones.
05:58 Maya: perfect, that helps our quality monitoring to create regression alerts.
06:05 Jules: performance acceptance criteria — what's a pass for the pilot?
06:10 Jonas: i'd say: p95 latency under X ms for the top 90% of traffic, overall throughput of Y requests/sec, and less than Z% error rate. we will formalize numbers once we see the sample traffic.
06:25 Liam: can you put that into a small benchmark spreadsheet? we can use that to evaluate.
06:30 Jonas: yes i'll produce a baseline sheet after the first test.
06:36 Maya: recap — Maya to send runbook and cost model (6/18), Jonas to coordinate perf bench and provide benchmark sheet, Nate to share staging network, Sofia to supply prompt set, Ravi to create CRM pilot ticket. any additions?
06:49 Ava: just one — please include an example of RBAC roles and admin flows for our SREs.
06:55 Maya: we'll include an RBAC appendix.
07:00 Jules: ok sounds like a plan. next meeting after the benchmark results — shall we aim for 6/25?
07:06 Ravi: 6/25 works; we'll tentatively book and confirm after test scheduling.
07:12 Maya: thanks everyone — i'll follow up with docs and links.
